mainTopic: Who the משנה about slaughtering on שבת for the wrong purpose describes (עוקר or טועה), and רבי יהושע's exemption for one who errs while doing a מצוה.
overview: The גמרא asks what kind of person the משנה describes when someone slaughters on שבת for the wrong purpose. It concludes that the רישא (a פסח slaughtered for another purpose) is about someone who did it deliberately (עוקר). The סיפא (other offerings slaughtered as a פסח) is about someone who made a mistake (טועה). רבי אבין accepts this split reading, and רבי אבהו teaches the same reading to רב יצחק בר יוסף, who reviews it forty times. The גמרא then asks how רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר can compare two halves that describe different people. It answers that רבי אליעזר sees no difference between them, while רבי יהושע gave one answer by his own view and another by רבי אליעזר's view. Next comes רבי יהושע's claim that communal offerings differ because they have a fixed number (קצבה). The גמרא challenges this from a case of two babies due for מילה, and רבי אמי answers that the man there was still busy with a waiting מצוה. A ברייתא of רבי חייא in the name of רבי מאיר then challenges רבי אמי, and that ברייתא itself seems to contradict itself. The school of רבי ינאי begins to resolve this by redefining its first case, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What case is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what exact situation the משנה describes when it says someone slaughtered the פסח on שבת for a different purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: With what case are we dealing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its whole discussion by asking what exact situation the משנה has in mind. The next steps will test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that someone who slaughters a פסח שלא לשמו on שבת is חייב חטאת. A person could slaughter it 'for a different purpose' in two ways. He could do it on purpose, knowing it is a פסח, or he could do it by mistake, thinking it was a different offering. The גמרא wants to know which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
With what case are we dealing? (a standard question asking for the exact situation)
Not for its own sake, meaning slaughtered with intent for a different type of offering

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With what are we dealing?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the first part of the משנה: someone who slaughtered the פסח on שבת for a different purpose.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the person in the רישא of the משנה changed the offering's purpose deliberately (עוקר) or by mistake (טועה).

steps.title: If he made a mistake, the משנה would be deciding a disputed question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the option that the person was mistaken (טועה). That reading would mean the משנה rules that a mistaken change of purpose still counts, which is surprising.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is dealing with someone who made a mistake, then learn from this that uprooting (changing the offering's purpose) by mistake counts as uprooting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, that the person thought the animal was a different offering. It then points out an unwanted consequence of that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is only חייב חטאת if the פסח became invalid. If he only changed its purpose by accident, the משנה would be teaching that עקירה בטעות still disqualifies the קרבן. That question is debated elsewhere by אמוראים (as תוספות notes), so it is unlikely that our משנה quietly settles it. That is why this option is pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to test)
One who is mistaken; here, he thought the animal was a different offering
Uprooting, meaning changing the offering's designated purpose
You learn from it (shows what would follow from this reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Being טועה here does not mean he did not know it was שבת. It means he was mistaken about which offering this animal was, so his 'different purpose' happened without real intent.

phrases.english: If you say it is with one who erred —
phrases.notes: He thought it was a different offering, not a פסח.

phrases.english: learn from it
phrases.notes: Learn from the fact that he is חייב, which means the פסח became invalid.

phrases.english: that uprooting by mistake is considered uprooting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question of step 1 and finds a problem with it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the רישא deals with a טועה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would force the משנה to rule that עקירה בטעות הויא עקירה, a matter that is disputed elsewhere.

steps.title: So the first case must be someone who changed the purpose on purpose
steps.stepSummary: Having rejected the mistaken-person reading, the גמרא concludes that the רישא deals with someone who deliberately uprooted the פסח's purpose (עוקר).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is dealing with one who deliberately uprooted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer to the opening question: the first case in the משנה is about a person who knew it was a פסח and deliberately slaughtered it for a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a deliberate change of purpose, everyone agrees the פסח becomes invalid. Slaughtering it was therefore not a מצוה, and he has desecrated שבת and owes a חטאת. This reading avoids the disputed question about mistakes.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the corrected answer)
One who deliberately uproots, meaning he intentionally changes the offering's purpose

phrases.english: Rather, it is with one who uprooted (deliberately).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 2 with the alternative.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רישא deals with an עוקר, someone who deliberately changed the פסח's purpose.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה does not fit a deliberate change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא, which distinguishes between animals fit and unfit to be a פסח. That distinction only makes sense if the person was mistaken, not if he deliberately changed the purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the latter clause: 'And all other offerings that he slaughtered for the sake of a פסח: if they are not fit, he is liable; if they are fit, רבי אליעזר holds him liable to a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.' Now if this is someone who deliberately uprooted, what difference does it make to me whether they are fit or not fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 3 by reading the next part of the משנה. If the whole משנה is about deliberate changes, the סיפא does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע exempts the person when the animal was fit to be a פסח. The reason is that the person honestly thought he was doing a מצוה, which only works if he was mistaken. A person who deliberately treats a different offering as a פסח has no such excuse, so fit or unfit should make no difference. Since the משנה does distinguish, the סיפא must be about a טועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause (we quote the end of the משנה to test the reading)
Fit, meaning the animal could have qualified as a פסח (for example, a male lamb in its first year)
Sin-offering, brought for accidentally breaking שבת
What difference is it to me? (a rhetorical challenge saying the distinction is pointless)

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
And all other offerings
that one slaughtered for the sake of the פסח,
if they are not fit — he is liable,
if they are fit —
Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable to a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.
Now if it is with one who uprooted (deliberately),
what difference is it to me if they are fit,
what difference is it to me if they are not fit?
phrases.notes: A deliberate actor has no excuse of 'I thought I was doing a מצוה' in either case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3 by showing that the עוקר reading cannot explain the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה deals with an עוקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא makes the law depend on whether the animals were fit. That distinction only matters for a mistaken person who thought he was doing a מצוה, not for someone who deliberately changed the purpose.

steps.title: The second half must be about someone who made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that the סיפא must be dealing with a טועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it is dealing with one who erred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the force of the challenge: the second case in the משנה can only be about someone who was mistaken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a mistaken person can say he thought he was doing a מצוה. That claim is what lets רבי יהושע exempt him when the animal was fit. So the סיפא is clearly about a טועה. This fixes the סיפא but creates a new problem for the משנה as a whole.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is with one who erred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the conclusion forced by the challenge of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סיפא deals with a טועה.

steps.title: The two halves of the משנה now describe different people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה now seems uneven: the רישא is about an עוקר while the סיפא is about a טועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is about one who uprooted deliberately and the latter clause is about one who erred?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an awkward result: the first half and second half of the same משנה would be talking about two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we expect both clauses of a משנה to describe the same type of situation. Step 3 forced the רישא to be about an עוקר, and step 5 forced the סיפא to be about a טועה. The גמרא questions whether such a split reading is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
The first clause is one case and the latter clause is another (a formula for a split reading)

phrases.english: The first clause is with one who uprooted (deliberately)
and the latter clause is with one who erred?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the results of steps 3 and 5 and points out that they clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: The overall reading of the משנה that results from steps 3 and 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is unlikely that a single משנה switches from a deliberate actor to a mistaken one without saying so.

steps.title: רבי אבין: Yes, the משנה really is split
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers that we accept the split reading: the רישא is about an עוקר and the סיפא is about a טועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: Yes, the first clause is about one who uprooted deliberately and the latter clause is about one who erred.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין answers the challenge by agreeing to it. The משנה really does switch cases between its two halves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rather than finding a way to make both halves match, רבי אבין says the evidence forces the split, so we accept it. The רישא avoids the disputed question of עקירה בטעות by being about an עוקר. The סיפא, which turns on a מצוה-mistake, must be about a טועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic), accepting the point of the challenge

steps.whatToRemember: The final reading of the משנה is that the רישא (a פסח slaughtered for another purpose) deals with an עוקר, while the סיפא (other offerings slaughtered as a פסח) deals with a טועה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said:
Yes,
the first clause is with one who uprooted (deliberately)
and the latter clause is with one who erred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 6 by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the split: the challenge is acknowledged as correct, and the משנה is read as covering two different kinds of cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the משנה should describe the same kind of person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about an עוקר and the סיפא is about a טועה.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר יוסף asks רבי אבהו about the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב יצחק בר יוסף finds רבי אבהו standing in a crowd and asks him how to explain the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף found רבי אבהו standing in a crowd of people. He said to him: What is the meaning of our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that confirms the same explanation. This step sets up the question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר יוסף asks his question even in a busy public setting, which shows how puzzling this משנה was. The question is the same one the גמרא has been working through: what case each half of the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him
A crowd or multitude (borrowed from Greek)
Our משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef found
Rabbi Abbahu
who was standing
in a crowd of people,
he said to him:
What is (the explanation of) our משנה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will confirm the explanation given by רבי אבין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to explain the cases of the משנה.

steps.title: רבי אבהו gives the same split explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers: the רישא is about an עוקר and the סיפא is about a טועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The first clause is about one who uprooted deliberately and the latter clause is about one who erred.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers with exactly the same explanation as רבי אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate אמוראים reach the same reading, which strengthens it. The unusual split is not a forced last resort. It is the accepted understanding of the משנה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The first clause is with one who uprooted (deliberately)
and the latter clause is with one who erred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רֵישָׁא בְּעוֹקֵר וְסֵיפָא בְּטוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רישא is about an עוקר and the סיפא is about a טועה.

steps.title: He reviewed it forty times until it was secure
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reviewed the explanation forty times until it felt as secure as something in his pocket.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learned it from him forty times, and it seemed to him as if it were resting in his pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by describing how רב יצחק בר יוסף reviewed this explanation many times until he knew it completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty reviews shows how hard this split reading is to hold onto: it is easy to forget that the two halves describe different people. The image of something 'in his pocket' means the knowledge became secure and always ready to use.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty times
His pocket or pouch

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is split: the רישא deals with an עוקר (deliberate change of purpose) and the סיפא deals with a טועה (mistaken person). This reading was confirmed by both רבי אבין and רבי אבהו, and it is worth reviewing until it is clear.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story teaches a lesson about learning: a confusing point should be reviewed many times until it becomes clear and secure.

phrases.english: He learned it from him
forty times
and it seemed to him
as if it were resting in his pocket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by describing how the answer of step 9 was mastered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The split reading (רישא בעוקר, סיפא בטועה) is the established explanation of the משנה, mastered through repeated review.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's comparison seems to undo the split reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from the משנה. It argues that if the רישא is about an עוקר and the סיפא is about a טועה, he could not have compared them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה that רבי אליעזר said: If a פסח, which is allowed to be slaughtered on שבת for its own purpose, still makes a person liable when he changed its purpose, then other offerings, which are not allowed on שבת even for their own purpose, should surely make him liable when he changed their purpose! But if the split reading is correct, these cases are not alike. The first part is about someone who deliberately uprooted the animal's purpose, and the second part is about someone who made a mistake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבין's split reading of the משנה. It uses רבי אליעזר's own argument as the evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works when the two cases are alike in the relevant way. If the פסח case involves a deliberate עוקר and the other-offerings case involves an honest טועה, then 'the פסח is liable, so all the more the others' falls apart. So the split reading seems to make רבי אליעזר's argument nonsense.

keyTerms.meaning: The Paschal lamb
He changed its purpose (slaughtered it as a different offering)
Other animal offerings
But these are not alike!

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted for its own purpose' means permitted to be slaughtered on שבת. A פסח may be slaughtered on שבת. Other private offerings may not.

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Eliezer said:
If a Paschal lamb, which is permitted (on Shabbat) for its own purpose,
when he changed its purpose, he is liable,
then offerings that are forbidden (on Shabbat) even for their own purpose,
when he changed their purpose,
is it not logical that he should be liable!
And if it is so (the split reading), these are not alike,
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own objection, beginning here.

phrases.english: since the first clause is about one who uprooted, and the latter clause is about one who erred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רישא/סיפא split that רבי אבין and רבי אבהו established.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the רישא is about an עוקר and the סיפא is about a טועה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר treats the two clauses as comparable cases. A split into deliberate uprooting and honest error would make them incomparable.

steps.title: For רבי אליעזר there is no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does not distinguish between an עוקר and a טועה, so his comparison still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, there is no difference between the two cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the split reading. In רבי אליעזר's view, uprooting and erring lead to the same result, so he can compare them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that someone who makes a mistake while trying to do a מצוה is still liable. So for him, the difference between an עוקר and a טועה does not matter. The difference exists in the משנה's structure, but it does not matter in his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes no difference to him
One who errs while doing a מצוה (רבי אליעזר holds him liable)

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, it makes no difference to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the difference to one opinion: the distinction is real, but רבי אליעזר does not accept it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר requires the two clauses to have the same kind of liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר, a טועה is liable just like an עוקר, so the comparison stands.

steps.title: Then why didn't רבי יהושע answer with this difference?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע does accept the difference, so he should have used it to refute רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יהושע, who does see a difference, let him answer רבי אליעזר this way!
steps.whatsHappening: Having fixed the problem for רבי אליעזר, the גמרא raises a new problem for רבי יהושע. Why did he give a different answer in the משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע rejects the קל וחומר by saying the פסח was changed into something forbidden while the other offerings were changed into something permitted. If the real difference for him is עוקר versus טועה, that would have been the simpler refutation. So why didn't he say it?

keyTerms.meaning: For whom it makes a difference
Let him answer him this way

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehoshua, for whom there is a difference,
let him answer him this way!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּשָׁנֵי לֵיהּ, לִישַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 12's answer and turns the question to רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's chosen reply in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהושע accepts the עוקר/טועה distinction, he should have used it to refute the קל וחומר instead of a different argument.

steps.title: רבי יהושע gives two answers: one for himself, one for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע meant: for me the cases are not alike (עוקר vs. טועה). But even by your view, the פסח was changed into something forbidden and the other offerings into something permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יהושע was saying to him: According to me, the cases are not alike, because the first part is about someone who uprooted and the second part is about someone who erred. But according to you: No! If you say this about a פסח, whose purpose he changed into something forbidden, would you say it about other offerings, whose purpose he changed into something permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יהושע really holds the עוקר/טועה difference. He also added a second answer that works even if you accept רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling רבי אליעזר 'I make a distinction' would not convince him, since he does not accept it. So רבי יהושע argued on רבי אליעזר's own terms. Turning a פסח into a regular offering on שבת creates a forbidden act. Turning a regular offering into a פסח creates something that is permitted on שבת, so that mistake is more understandable.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant to say to him
According to me / according to you
No, if you said (the standard formula for rejecting a קל וחומר)
Something forbidden / something permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common style of argument: give your own reason first, then refute your opponent on his own premises.

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
According to me, they are not alike,
the first clause is about one who uprooted and the latter clause about one who erred.
According to you: No, if you said this about a Paschal lamb
whose purpose he changed to something forbidden,
would you say it about other offerings
whose purpose he changed to something permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה: רבי יהושע's words contain two answers, one by his own view and one by his opponent's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע ignored the עוקר/טועה distinction and argued something else.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds the distinction himself. The forbidden/permitted argument was aimed at רבי אליעזר, who rejects the distinction.
steps.whatToRemember: The split reading (רישא is an עוקר, סיפא is a טועה) survives. רבי אליעזר ignores the distinction, and רבי יהושע uses it but adds a second argument for רבי אליעזר's sake.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings communal offerings as proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר points to communal offerings. They may be slaughtered on שבת for their own purpose, yet a person who slaughters other animals as communal offerings is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: Let the communal offerings prove it! They are allowed on שבת for their own purpose, and yet one who slaughters other animals for their purpose is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate in the משנה continues. רבי אליעזר brings a case to show that a permitted target purpose does not exempt the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had argued that changing an offering into a פסח is changing it into something permitted, so the person should be exempt. רבי אליעזר answers that communal offerings are also permitted on שבת, yet someone who slaughters other animals as communal offerings on שבת is liable. So 'changed into something permitted' is not a reason to exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings (here meaning the communal sacrifices offered on שבת)
Will prove it
One who slaughters (other animals) for their purpose

steps.confusionAlert: 'והשוחט לשמן' does not mean slaughtering the real communal offerings. It means slaughtering other animals as if they were communal offerings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
Let communal offerings prove it,
for they are permitted (on Shabbat) for their own purpose,
and one who slaughters (other animals) for their purpose is liable,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's debate, answering רבי יהושע's forbidden/permitted argument quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That changing an offering's purpose to something permitted on שבת still makes the person liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of slaughtering animals as communal offerings on שבת, where the person is liable.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: communal offerings have a fixed limit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the proof. Communal offerings have a fixed number, so an extra one is clearly wrong. The פסח has no fixed number, so a mistake about it is understandable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No! If you said this about communal offerings, that is because they have a fixed limit. Would you say it about the פסח, which has no fixed limit?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back on רבי אליעזר's proof by showing that communal offerings are a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings have a set number each day, so anyone slaughtering an extra one should know it is not needed. That is why he is liable. The פסח has no set number, since any person can bring one, so someone who mistakenly treats an animal as a פסח has a good excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed limit or set number
Because (it is so that)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's final distinction is קצבה. Where there is a fixed number, a mistake has no excuse. With the פסח, which has no fixed number, the mistake is understandable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
No, if you said this about communal offerings,
that is because they have a fixed limit,
would you say it about the Paschal lamb, which has no fixed limit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between communal offerings and the פסח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Communal offerings have a fixed number, so an extra one cannot be an honest mistake. The פסח has no fixed number, so a mistake about it is excusable.

steps.title: Babies also have a fixed number, yet רבי יהושע exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יהושע holds a person liable wherever there is a fixed number. In the משנה about two babies needing מילה, there is a fixed number, yet רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that wherever there is a fixed number, רבי יהושע holds the person liable? But babies have a fixed number, and we learned in a משנה: A man had two babies. One was due for מילה after שבת and one was due on שבת. He forgot and circumcised the after-שבת baby on שבת. He is liable. Now suppose one baby was due on ערב שבת and one was due on שבת, and he forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. רבי אליעזר obligates him to bring a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason רבי יהושע just gave, that communal offerings are different because they have a fixed number. It brings a case with a fixed number where רבי יהושע still exempts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each baby has exactly one מילה, so the number is fixed, just like communal offerings. Still, when the man mixed up the babies, רבי יהושע exempts him. So a fixed number alone cannot be what makes רבי יהושע say the person is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, limited number
Babies (here, baby boys waiting for their ברית מילה)
To circumcise him
A sin offering, brought for breaking שבת by mistake
Friday, the day before שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two baby cases apart. In the first case, the baby he circumcised was not due yet (after שבת), so there was no מצוה at all and everyone agrees he is liable. In the second case, the baby was already overdue (from ערב שבת), so a מצוה was still done. Only the second case has a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Is that to say that wherever

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִית לֵיהּ קִצְבָה מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ?
phrases.english: there is a fixed number, Rabbi Yehoshua holds him liable?
But there are babies, which have a fixed number,
phrases.notes: Each baby gets exactly one מילה.

phrases.english: and we learned in a Mishnah: one who had two babies,
one to be circumcised after Shabbat
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,

phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the after-Shabbat one on Shabbat
he is liable.
phrases.notes: That baby was not yet due, so no מצוה was done.

phrases.english: If one was to be circumcised on Shabbat eve,
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat
Rabbi Eliezer obligates him to bring a sin offering,
phrases.notes: A late מילה does not push aside שבת.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ קִצְבָה מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning רבי יהושע used in step 16 (fixed number means liable).
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle from step 16 that רבי יהושע holds someone liable wherever there is a קצבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Babies needing מילה have a קצבה, yet רבי יהושע exempts the one who mixed them up. So קצבה cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: רבי אמי: with the babies, he was still busy with a real מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that in the baby case, the man circumcised the wrong baby first, while the שבת baby was still waiting. Since he was busy with a real מצוה, his mistake is excused. In the offerings case, the required communal offerings were already slaughtered, so there was no reason for confusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he first circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת, while the שבת baby was still there and he was busy with him. Here, with the offerings, it is a case where he had already slaughtered the communal offerings at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the challenge. He shows that the baby case and the offerings case differ in a key detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the babies, a real מצוה was still waiting (the שבת baby), so the man was rushing and busy, and an honest mix-up makes sense. With the offerings, the fixed communal offerings were already finished, so nothing was waiting and there was no reason to slaughter more. The fixed number still matters, but only once it has already been filled.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? A formula that narrows a source to a specific situation
That he went first, i.e., he did this one before the other
Busy or preoccupied (with a מצוה)
Communal offerings (literally, the parts of the community's offerings burned on the מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a mistake made while busy with a real, still-pending מצוה is treated more gently than a mistake made after the מצוה is already finished.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
With what case are we dealing here?
In a case where he first circumcised
the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat,
when that Shabbat baby was still there, and he was busy with him.
phrases.notes: A real מצוה was still waiting, so his rush and confusion are understandable.

phrases.english: Here, it is a case where he first slaughtered
the communal offerings at the beginning.
phrases.notes: Nothing was left to do, so there was no reason to slaughter more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by limiting each source to a specific situation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case differentiation (אוקימתא): the order of events determines whether the person was busy with a pending מצוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Babies and communal offerings both have a fixed number, so רבי יהושע should rule the same way in both.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the babies, the שבת baby was still waiting, so the man was busy with a מצוה and is exempt. With the offerings, the required ones were already done, so he is liable.

steps.title: Then רבי מאיר's ruling would exempt even when nothing was left to do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי's answer. In the משנה, רבי מאיר says that one who slaughters for the sake of communal offerings is exempt. By רבי אמי's reading, this would have to mean he is exempt even after the communal offerings were already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי מאיר says: Even one who slaughters for the sake of communal offerings is exempt. That would mean he is exempt even though he had already slaughtered the communal offerings at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to רבי אמי. It shows that his reading forces an extreme position onto רבי מאיר, and the next step brings the source that makes this a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said the person in the offerings case is liable because the communal offerings were already done. So when רבי מאיר says that person is exempt, רבי מאיר must hold he is exempt even when nothing was left to do. That is a very lenient view, and the גמרא is about to test it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a formula that tests what follows from the last answer
Exempt (from bringing a חטאת)
At the beginning, first

phrases.english: If so,
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם אֵימוּרֵי צִיבּוּר פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: even one who slaughters for the sake of communal offerings is exempt,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's report of רבי יהושע's view in the משנה.

phrases.english: even though he had already slaughtered
the communal offerings at the beginning?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי? רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם אֵימוּרֵי צִיבּוּר פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי אמי's answer from step 18 against רבי מאיר's statement in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's reading that the offerings case involves communal offerings already finished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, רבי מאיר exempts even when no מצוה was left to do. This sets up a contradiction with רבי מאיר's view on the babies, brought in the next step.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ברייתא: רבי מאיר says everyone holds liable in the baby case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי חייא from אבל ערב. In it, רבי מאיר says רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that the man who circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת is liable. This clashes with the lenient view רבי אמי's reading gives רבי מאיר for the offerings case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא from אבל ערב taught that רבי מאיר said: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not disagree about a man who had two babies, one due for מילה on ערב שבת and one due on שבת, who forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. Both agree he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that powers its challenge against רבי אמי. Step 21 finishes quoting this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the baby case, the שבת baby was still waiting, so the man was busy with a real מצוה. Even so, רבי מאיר says everyone holds him liable. It makes no sense for רבי מאיר to be strict there but lenient in the offerings case, where, by רבי אמי's reading, nothing was left to do.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not disagree; both agree on this case
The village of אבל ערב, home of this רבי חייא

steps.confusionAlert: In the משנה, the baby case is a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. In רבי מאיר's version, brought by רבי חייא, both agree he is liable. These are two different versions of the same מחלוקת.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiya [from Avel Arav] teach in a baraita:
Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree
about one who had two babies,
one to be circumcised on Shabbat eve
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat
that he is liable.
phrases.notes: Both agree, even though the שבת baby was still waiting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַתַּנְיָא, רַבִּי חִיָּיא מֵאָבֵל עֲרָב אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge set up in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge against רבי אמי's reading, which makes רבי מאיר exempt even when no מצוה was left to do.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא from אבל ערב, in which רבי מאיר says both sides hold liable in the case of the ערב שבת baby circumcised on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's answer (step 18), which forces רבי מאיר's version of רבי יהושע to exempt even after the communal offerings were finished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבי חייא's ברייתא, רבי מאיר reports that even רבי יהושע holds liable in the ערב שבת baby case, where the man was still busy with the waiting שבת baby. It is inconsistent for רבי מאיר's רבי יהושע to be strict there yet lenient in the offerings case, where by רבי אמי's reading nothing was left to do.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא: where the two תנאים disagree
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to say where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע do argue. The case is a man who forgot and circumcised the after-שבת baby on שבת. רבי אליעזר makes him bring a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did they argue about? About a man who had two babies to circumcise, one after שבת and one on שבת. He forgot and circumcised the after-שבת baby on שבת. רבי אליעזר says he must bring a חטאת, and רבי יהושע says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא of רבי חייא from Step 20. Now it gives the second half, which tells us the case where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first half (Step 20), both agreed the man is liable. In this second half, the man circumcised a baby who was not yet eight days old, so no מצוה applied to that baby at all. Even so, רבי יהושע exempts him, because he was busy with the general מצוה of מילה when he made the mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: they disagreed
babies
to circumcise
he forgot (acted by mistake)
sin-offering brought for an accidental sin
exempts

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About one who had two babies,
one to be circumcised after Shabbat
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the after-Shabbat one on Shabbat,
for Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable to a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that was started in Step 20, giving its second half.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge to רבי אמי's reading of רבי מאיר, by showing what רבי מאיר reports about רבי יהושע's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא from אבל ערב, second half.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can be right. If רבי יהושע exempts the man when he did no מצוה at all, how could he hold him liable when he did a real מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really understand it this way? There, where he did not do a מצוה, רבי יהושע exempts him. And here, where he did do a מצוה, would רבי יהושע hold him liable?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two halves of the ברייתא do not seem to fit together in רבי יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first half, the ערב שבת baby was already obligated in מילה, so circumcising him was a real מצוה, and yet רבי יהושע agrees the man is liable. In the second half, the after-שבת baby was not yet obligated, so there was no מצוה at all, and yet רבי יהושע exempts him. That is backwards: the case with the real מצוה should get the more lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a phrase of surprise that sets up a challenge)
there (in the other case)
he did a מצוה
where, in a case where
holds liable

steps.confusionAlert: The "ערב שבת baby" is a baby whose eighth day was Friday. Circumcising him is a real מצוה, but a late מילה does not override שבת. That is why doing it on שבת can still make a person liable.

phrases.english: And can you understand it this way?
If there, where he did not perform a מצוה,
Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him,
then where he did perform a מצוה, would he hold him liable?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal logic of the ברייתא just quoted in Steps 20 and 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's presentation of רבי יהושע's view: liable in the first half, exempt in the second half.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר-style objection. If he is exempt where no מצוה was done, he should surely be exempt where a real מצוה was done.

steps.title: The school of רבי ינאי: the first half is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the first half of the ברייתא describes an unusual situation. The man had first circumcised the שבת baby early, on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: The first half is about a case where he went ahead and circumcised the שבת baby on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to the contradiction by redefining the case in the first half of the ברייתא. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the man had a ערב שבת baby and a שבת baby. By mistake he circumcised the שבת baby early, on Friday, and then circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. This special setup will explain why even רבי יהושע holds him liable there, even though a מצוה was done.

keyTerms.meaning: the scholars of the school of רבי ינאי said
the first clause
for example, as in a case where
he went ahead, did it first
Friday, the day before שבת

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
The first clause is where he went ahead first
and circumcised the Shabbat baby on Shabbat eve,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the first clause as a special scenario.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first half seemed to be an ordinary case of circumcising the ערב שבת baby on שבת, which would contradict רבי יהושע's leniency in the second half.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first half is a special case where the שבת baby had already been circumcised early on ערב שבת. The explanation continues on the next amud.
